title: Schematic image of a quasi-affine open after etale base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T,T'$ be affine schemes over $S$, let $a:T'\to T$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with a morphism $f:X\to T$. Suppose that for every representable etale map $h_V\to X$ with $V$ a scheme the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and that the diagonal $X\to X\times_TX$ becomes a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $V'\subseteq X\times_TT'$ be an open subspace represented by a scheme, and suppose $V'\to T'$ is quasi-affine: it factors as a quasi-compact open immersion into a scheme affine over $T'$. An open subspace means a subfunctor whose inclusion becomes an open immersion on scheme base changes [def-weil-open-immersion]; quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover, and affine over $T'$ means that inverse images of affine opens are affine schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Then the image of $|V'|$ in $|X|$ is the underlying set of a quasi-compact open subspace $W\subseteq X$ represented by a scheme. Here $|X|$ is the set of field-valued point classes. A field-valued point class means a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ with $K$ a field, with two such maps identified when they agree over a common field extension; the underlying set of an open subspace is the set of classes that factor through it.

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_TT'$ and let $r:X'\to X$ be the projection. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], $r$ is representable etale. The open inclusion $V'\to X'$ is representable etale: on every scheme base change it is an open immersion, hence etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. So $q:V'\to X$ is representable etale by the same permanence node. As $T'$ is affine, the given quasi-compact open immersion of $V'$ goes into an affine scheme by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; so $V'$ is quasi-compact. [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] applied to $q$ gives a quasi-compact open subspace $W\subseteq X$ with $|W|=q(|V'|)$. It remains to prove $W$ a scheme.

For $n\geq0$ let $P(n)$ assert this for every diagram of the statement (all $S,T,T',X,V'$) whose $a$ has fibre degrees bounded by $n$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. The map $a$ is locally quasi-finite: each etale scheme chart of $T'$ has etale composite to $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite], applied to $T'$ and its identity chart, gives it. Its source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] gives such an $n$. Use strong induction. If $n=0$, every fibre has zero coordinate algebra, so is empty; each point of $T'$ lies in its fibre, so $T'=V'=\varnothing$ and $W$ is the empty scheme. Fix $n\geq1$ and assume $P(m)$ for $m<n$.

For $n\geq1$, apply [lem-a1-affine-etale-diagonal-complement-degree]. It gives affine $T^*=(T'\times_TT')\setminus\Delta(T')$ and etale $b=\pi_1|_{T^*}$ of fibre degree at most $n-1$. If $n=1$, it makes $a$ an open immersion. Its scheme base changes are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], hence so is $X'\to X$ on scheme tests; $W$ is then the scheme $V'$.

For $n>1$, use [lem-a1-etale-saturation-quasi-affine-pullback] with $Z=p_0^{-1}(V')\cap(X\times_TT^*)$. Its first conclusion verifies all remaining hypotheses of $P(n-1)$ for $(T',T^*,X',Z)$, with $\pi_0$ defining $Z$ and $\pi_1$ defining $b$. Induction supplies its quasi-compact schematic image $H\subseteq X'$. The same node now identifies $W\times_TT'=V'\cup H$ and makes it a quasi-compact scheme quasi-affine over $T'$.

Apply [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] to $a$ to obtain its open image $B$. The image of $W$ in $T$ lies in $B$, since every point of $W$ comes from $V'$ and $V'\to T$ factors through $T'$. Apply [lem-a1-open-image-quasi-affine-scheme-descent] to the quasi-affine pullback just obtained: it represents $W$ by a scheme over $B$, hence over $S$. This proves $P(n)$; strong induction and the chosen bound complete the proof.

lean.statement: theorem etale_quasiAffine_image_scheme {S : Scheme.{u}} (T T' : Over S) [IsAffine T.left] [IsAffine T'.left] (a : T' ⟶ T) [Etale a.left] (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hlocal : ∀ (U : Over S) (g : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (q : U ⟶ T), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale g → yoneda.map q = g ≫ f → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite q.left) (hdiag : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (Limits.pullback.diagonal f)) (V' : Over S) (v : yoneda.obj V' ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : V' ⟶ T') (hcomm : v ≫ f = yoneda.map b ≫ yoneda.map a) (hvopen : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (Limits.pullback.lift v (yoneda.map b) hcomm)) (hvquasi : ∃ (Y : Over S) (j : V' ⟶ Y) (c : Y ⟶ T'), j ≫ c = b ∧ IsOpenImmersion j.left ∧ QuasiCompact j.left ∧ IsAffineHom c.left) : ∃ (W : Over S) (w : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), CompactSpace W.left ∧ AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) w ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (g : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsFieldSpectrum U → (FieldPointImage U g V' v ↔ FieldPointImage U g W w)
